0. FOREWORD

0.1 This Indian Standard ( Second Revision ) was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 24 October 1980, after the draft finalized by the Metal Containers Sectional Committee had been approved by the Marine, Cargo Movement and Packaging Division Council. 0.2 This standard has been updated to bring it in line with IS : 21341972* and incorporate the requirements for cans with handles which are very much in vogue. 0.3 The cans conforming to this standard are suitable for liquid paints ( insoluble pigment products ) of the following varieties: a) Air-drying type paints, enamels, undercoats and primers ( oil or synthetic base ); b) Stoving c) Emulsion finishes, undercoats and and lacquers, and primers ( oil or synthetic-base ); type paints;

d) Nitrocellulose 1. SCOPE 1.1 This standard nominal capacity liquid paints. 2. TERMINOLOGY

and spirit enamels

APPENDIX
( Clause 2.1.2 )
DETERMINATION Gross procedure: lidded capacity

A

OF GROSS LIDDED shall be determined

CAPACITY by the following

.

a) Drill two 8 mm diameter holes in the bottom to one another and remove the burrs.

of the can adjacent

b) Fit all the closure components (just as though the can had been filled ), being careful to ensure that none is omitted. Ensure that the closure is correctly driven home. Weigh the closed, empty can in grams ( ml ). c) With the closed can tilt@ slightly, fill it through one of the holes with water at a temperature of 2O"C, using a narrow jet. When water first runs out of the second hole, complete filling is ensured by closing the holes with the fingers, gently shaking the can, removing the fingers from the holes and completing the filling. Carefully remove all surface water.
NOTE An alternative method of filling the closed can is as follows: D$i\l_two 8 mm diameter holes in the bottom of the can, diametrically opposite one another and each as close as possible to thr circl!mference of the bottom Immerse the can bottom upwarda. in a buckrt or tank of Tilt slightly to dispel anv residual clean water at room temperature. air pocket. Withdraw the can vertically and carefully remove all surface water.

9

IS t 1407 - 1980
d) Weigh the filled can in grams ( ml ). The difference two weighings ( ms - ml ) represents the capacity in millilitres. between the of the can

e) Report the value obtained to the nearest millilitre rounding down to the nearest whole millilitre if the decimal fraction is below 0.5 and up to the nearest whole millilitre if the decimal fraction is O-5 or greater.

APPENDIX ( Clause 10.1 )
LEAKAGE TEST
The leakage test shall be carried out as follows:

a) Take the can without its closure and place over the open end a rubber-faced sealing plate equipped with the means of introducing air into the can and a pressure gauge capable of measuring 15 kPa. b) Pump air into the can until the gauge reads 15 kPa and immerse the can in water until it is just below the surface of the liquid. c) Leave the can in the leakage. The presence stream of bubbles. water for 15 seconds and of any leakage is indicated examine for by a steady
